concepts.learning_objective: Define a right as an entitlement or justified claim and distinguish it from a mere want.
Explain dignity and well-being as grounds on which rights are claimed, and why harmful activities cannot be rights.
Describe the seventeenth and eighteenth century theory of natural rights to life, liberty and property.
Explain the idea of universal human rights and how the list of human rights has expanded.
Explain Kant's moral conception of rights based on human dignity.
Explain why legal and constitutional recognition gives rights a special status without being their basis.
Explain how rights require the state to act in some ways and to refrain from acting in others.
Identify political rights and civil liberties and explain how they make government accountable.
Distinguish economic and cultural rights and explain why democracies recognise them.
Explain the obligations that rights place on individuals, including the common good and respect for the rights of others.
Evaluate how rights are balanced when they conflict and why citizens must be vigilant about restrictions on civil liberties.
